newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico accepts bids for tugboat concessions.
newsitem.headline: Mexico accepts bids for tugboat concessions.

text.p: Mexico received bids on Tuesday in the privatization of tugboat operations at three ports, the Communications and Transport ministry said.
The winners are to be announced on December 23.
Transportacion Maritima Mexicana (TMM) offered the highest bid of 38.25 million pesos to administer tugboats at the Manzanillo port in the state of Colima on the Pacific Coast.

Sudamericana Agencias Aereas y Maritimas (SAAM) offered 36.97 million pesos to operate tugboats at the Lazaro Cardenas port in the state of Michoacan on the Pacific Coast. The company offered a bid of 37.92 million pesos for the Manzanillo concession.

Local investment fund Fondo de Inversion Veracruz (FIVER) offered the highest bid -- 34.8 million pesos -- for the concession at Coatzacoalcos port in Veracruz state along the Gulf of Mexico. TMM offered a lower 23.71 million peso bid.
The winning bidders will be granted a 10-year concession to administer tugboat operations, the ministry said, as part of a larger effort to privatize operations of the nation's ports.
